userStories.title: Propagate call identifiers to command-safety shadow rows
acceptanceCriteria: When `openShadowTap` receives a Bash call with `callId: "c1"`, `scopeId: "s1"`, `turnId: "t1"`, `roundTrips: 2`, and `toolCallId: "tc1"`, then the Observation passed to `observe` carries those five values.

When `openShadowTap` receives an Exec call with `callId: "c1"`, `scopeId: "s1"`, `turnId: "t1"`, `roundTrips: 2`, and `toolCallId: "tc1"`, then the Observation passed to `observe` carries those five values.

When `openShadowTap` receives a Bash call with no identifiers, then the Observation passed to `observe` has none of the keys `callId`, `scopeId`, `turnId`, `roundTrips`, or `toolCallId` when checked with `in`.

Given a `createCommandShadow` with resolving `classify` and recording `write`, when it observes an Observation carrying all five identifiers and settles with `settle(key, { ledger: "ok" })`, then the single written row carries the same five values.
Given a `createCommandShadow`, when it observes an Observation with no identifiers and settles it, then the written row has none of the five identifier keys when checked with `in`.

When `runtime.callTool("Bash", …)` is created with `callId: "c1"` and `scopeId: "s1"` runtime options and called with context `turnId: "t1"`, `roundTrips: 3`, and `toolCallId: "tc1"`, then its recording command shadow observes those five values.
When that identified Bash runtime call is written to the runtime sink, then its tool-audit record carries the same `callId`, `turnId`, and `toolCallId` as its Observation.
When `runtime.callTool("Bash", …)` has no `callId`/`scopeId` options and no context, then its Observation has none of the five identifier keys when checked with `in`.
When an individual identifier source is undefined at the tap, then the resulting written row omits that identifier key rather than storing `undefined`.

routing.reasoning: Four existing modules receive only optional field plumbing using established conditional-spread and recording test seams; no new abstraction or behavior-changing policy path is introduced.

modifiedFiles.reason: fixtures without identifiers must still produce observations without the identifier keys; existing assertions are unchanged.
fixtures without identifiers must still produce rows without the identifier keys; existing assertions are unchanged.

userStories.title: Record wrapped sandbox argv in tool audit payloads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve the sandbox backend argv that actually ran alongside the unchanged logical executed argv.

**Motivation** — tool-audit never records the sandbox argv (review #13, MEDIUM).

**Approach** — `SandboxRecord` (`src/sandbox/types.ts`) gains:

```ts
/** Wrapped calls only: the argv the sandbox backend returned and runArgv executed. */
readonly argv?: readonly string[];
```

`runWrapped` sets `sandbox.argv` to the `argv` returned by `backend.wrap(...)`, the same array it passes to `runArgv`. `runUnwrapped` (disabled and unavailable states) never sets it: there `executed` is already what ran. `executed` keeps the logical argv on both paths. The Bash and Exec tools already pass `launched.sandbox` into `ToolResult.audit.sandbox`, and `runtime.callTool` spreads it into the tool-audit record, so no tool or runtime change is needed.

**Scope** — In: the optional SandboxRecord argv field, wrapped launcher result population, and compatible sandbox/audit assertions. Out: US-001 shadow identifiers; US-003 Exec shadow executed argv; `executed` on tool-audit rows keeps its meaning (the logical argv); no field is renamed or re-typed.; Redacting or truncating the sandbox argv (review #9 is a separate ruling).; US-002 only: the Linux bwrap path is covered by the same `runWrapped` code; no Linux-specific test is added. Do not add tests to `test/unit/tools/runtime.test.ts` (688 lines, already past the 650-line split target in `.nax/rules/test-architecture.md`; 800 is the hard limit); put new tests in this story's created test files.
acceptanceCriteria: When an available `createCommandLauncher` uses a fake backend whose `wrap` resolves `["sandbox-exec", "-p", "PROFILE", "/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"]` for shell request `echo hi`, then `sandbox.argv` equals that wrapped array.
When that wrapped shell call runs, then the recording `_launcherDeps.runArgv` receives `["sandbox-exec", "-p", "PROFILE", "/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"]` as `argv`.
When that wrapped shell call resolves, then `executed` equals `["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"]`, unchanged by this feature.
When an available-state launcher handles argv request `["bun", "test"]`, then it resolves with `executed` `["bun", "test"]` and `sandbox.argv` equal to the fake backend's wrapped array.
When a disabled-state launcher resolves, then `sandbox` equals `{ backend: "none", wrapped: false }` exactly with no `argv` key.
When an unavailable-state launcher resolves, then its `sandbox` has no `argv` key when checked with `in`.
When a wrapped launcher call exits non-zero with stderr matching the sandbox-denial pattern, then it resolves with both `denialHint: true` and `sandbox.argv` set.

When `runtime.callTool` runs a tool returning `audit: { executed: ["x"], sandbox: { backend: "srt", wrapped: true, argv: ["w", "x"] } }`, then the resulting tool-audit row contains `sandbox.argv` `["w", "x"]` and `executed` `["x"]`.
When `backend.wrap` throws, then `createCommandLauncher.run()` rejects with code `SANDBOX_WRAP_FAILED` and the recording `_launcherDeps.runArgv` receives no call.

routing.reasoning: The change spans the shared sandbox type and wrapped launch result, with existing injected launcher and runtime audit seams validating the propagated payload.

modifiedFiles.reason: an exact-equality assertion over a wrapped `LaunchResult.sandbox` may gain `argv`; the invariant kept is that `executed` equals the logical argv on every path.
an exact-equality assertion over `audit.sandbox` for a wrapped call may gain `argv`; `executed` assertions are unchanged.
an exact-equality assertion over `audit.sandbox` for a wrapped call may gain `argv`; `executed` assertions are unchanged.

outOfScope: redacting or truncating the sandbox argv

userStories.title: Record normalized Exec argv on shadow rows
acceptanceCriteria: When an Exec `openShadowTap` is settled with `("ok", undefined, ["bun", "run", "--filter", "pkg", "test"])`, then it calls the recording shadow's `settle` with that array as its third argument.
When a Bash `openShadowTap` is settled with `("ok", undefined, ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hi"])`, then it calls the recording shadow's `settle` with exactly two arguments.

Given a `createCommandShadow`, when it observes an Exec Observation with `argv: ["bun", "test"]` and settles with `settle(key, { ledger: "ok" }, ["bun", "test", "--no-scripts"])`, then the written row has `executed` `["bun", "test", "--no-scripts"]`, `argv` `["bun", "test"]`, and `command` `bun test`.
When that Exec Observation is classified, then `classify` is called with `bun test`, not the executed argv.
When a shadow entry is settled with no third argument, then its written row has no `executed` key when checked with `in`.
When a shadow entry is settled by `drain()` as `unsettled`, then its written row has no `executed` key when checked with `in`.

When `runtime.callTool` invokes the Exec identity through a coding tool with `scope.argvField` `argv` whose `run` returns `audit: { executed: ["bun", "test", "--no-scripts"] }`, then the recording command shadow settles with `{ ledger: "ok" }` and third argument `["bun", "test", "--no-scripts"]`.
When `runtime.callTool` denies an Exec call by policy, then the recording command shadow settles with `{ ledger: "denied" }` and no third argument or `undefined`.
When `runtime.callTool("Bash", { command: "echo hi" })` runs in raw mode with a recording command shadow, then it settles with exactly `[key, { ledger: "ok" }]` and no third argument.
When an Exec call is denied with outcome `denied:ask`, then its written shadow row has no `executed` key because the tool never ran.
When the Exec tool encounters a post-normalization launch error and returns through the runtime error path without audit data, then its written shadow row has no `executed` key.
When a recording shadow throws from `settle`, then `runtime.callTool` returns its normal tool outcome and the thrown shadow failure does not escape.

routing.reasoning: This is bounded optional-argument and row-state plumbing across four established modules, with explicit identity and error-path regressions but no new abstraction.

modifiedFiles.reason: Bash settle assertions (`toEqual([[key, { ledger: "ok" }]])`) stay exactly as they are; the recorder's `settle` may accept a third argument.

outOfScope: placing executed on Bash shadow rows

analysis:
This is an additive enhancement to existing command-safety, runtime audit, and sandbox-launcher flows. `runtime.callTool` opens a shadow tap after `policy.check` with a throwaway `randomUUID()` key and currently sends command, argv, verdict, stage, and storyId only (src/tools/runtime.ts:335-358). Its `log()` already conditionally records `callId`, `scopeId`, `turnId`, `roundTrips`, and `toolCallId` in ToolCallRecord (src/tools/runtime.ts:274-333), while `logCall` currently settles the tap with only ledger and `approval.decidedBy` (src/tools/runtime.ts:359-365). This is the required integration seam: pass the existing IDs to the tap and `args[8]?.executed` at settlement without changing the random tap key. ToolCallRecord defines the same five fields and join semantics (src/tools/tool-audit.ts:75-119), so shadow records must reuse them exactly.

The shadow is deliberately observational. `toObservation` converts `ShadowCall` to Bash or Exec observations, and `openShadowTap` catches both observe and settle failures (src/command-safety/tap.ts:31-78). `createCommandShadow` scores and classifies `obs.command`, joins model/outcome state, and serializes `toRow` (src/command-safety/shadow.ts:69-177). `Observation`, `CommandSafetyRow`, and `CommandShadow.settle` lack the requested fields today (src/command-safety/types.ts:57-104). Every new optional field must use conditional object spreads so absent sources create no key rather than an `undefined` key. For US-003, retain executed argv in the shadow Entry from settlement to `toRow`; keep `obs.command`, raw `obs.argv`, `scoreRules`, classifier input, and `shadowCacheKey` based on the model input. Tap forwarding must be identity-gated: even if runtime has audit.executed, Bash calls `shadow.settle` with two arguments only.

`logicalArgv` provides the logical shell/argv command, `runUnwrapped` executes and returns it, and `runWrapped` executes the `backend.wrap()` array but currently drops that array while returning logical `executed` (src/sandbox/launcher.ts:35-88). `SandboxRecord` has backend/wrapped/reason/denialHint but no argv (src/sandbox/types.ts:47-53); `LaunchResult.executed` explicitly means logical argv (src/sandbox/types.ts:72-76). US-002 adds wrapper argv only to successful wrapped results, including sandbox-denial results. Disabled and unavailable flows share `runUnwrapped` and must retain no `argv`; wrap failure must remain `SANDBOX_WRAP_FAILED` without a spawn/result. Bash and Exec already propagate `launched.sandbox` into audit and runtime already spreads `audit.sandbox` (src/tools/runtime.ts:304-307), so no production tool/runtime work is required for US-002. Exec's normalized argv is already returned in `audit.executed` only after a launch result; its catch path returns no audit (src/tools/run-command-exec.ts:64-116), providing the intended no-executed shadow outcome.

Relevant test seams are established: `tap.test.ts` records observe/settle tuples (test/unit/command-safety/tap.test.ts:12-164), `shadow.test.ts` has manual classification, captured rows, and drain coverage (test/unit/command-safety/shadow.test.ts:31-235), `runtime-command-shadow.test.ts` asserts raw Bash behavior and shadow isolation (test/unit/tools/runtime-command-shadow.test.ts:20-112), and `launcher.test.ts` injects runArgv and covers all sandbox states, wrap errors, and denial hints (test/unit/sandbox/launcher.test.ts:17-238). Exact sandbox assertions in launcher/Bash/Exec sandbox tests must be updated additively. `test/unit/tools/runtime.test.ts` is already 688 lines, above the 650-line split target, so new runtime tests belong in the specified new files.

Risks are semantic regression rather than migration: never replace or rename existing `executed`, never leak undefined keys, never classify normalized Exec argv, never attach executed to Bash rows, and never let a shadow error impact a call. JSONL schemas remain backward-compatible because all additions are optional; existing rows/readers need no migration and old data cannot be backfilled. US-003 depends on US-001 because both alter the tap/type/runtime shape and its specified seam consumes the identifier-bearing tap call.
outOfScope: `executed` on tool-audit rows keeps its meaning (the logical argv); no field is renamed or re-typed.
Classifying the normalized Exec argv instead of the model's argv is not done: it would split the policy/human/shadow byte-identity.
Redacting or truncating the sandbox argv (review #9 is a separate ruling).
Locking or bounding the command-safety / approval-audit JSONL (review #14).
`nax` CLI readers or reports of the new fields.
US-002 only: the Linux bwrap path is covered by the same `runWrapped` code; no Linux-specific test is added.
